rationale: The assistant immediately told the customer to unplug and never open the casing, asked the two right questions (metal, then the side-wall panel) and correctly identified the burnt waveguide cover as the cause, recommending a model-specific replacement, which is justified since the model was known. However the second turn is internally contradictory: the card says 'don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer' while the body tells them to fit the part themselves and 'test with a cup of water'. The numbered steps are garbled ('1. 2. 3. Remove it'), it never told them to clean the heavy grease splatter they described, and it gave no fallback if sparking persists after replacement.
